characters/npcs/brennan.html.title: Brennan
characters/npcs/brennan.html.description:
Leader of the Claws, the bandits that loom largest in Stonetop's recent memory.The Claws would shake down villagers when they caught them travelling, but Stonetop is largely too poor to bother with. They'd outright rob travelling traders, but to Stonetop they were more bullies than bandits.Their aggression escalated partly because of the arrival of Lenox and The Grateful. The Claws got wind that Stonetop was seeing a slight influx of foreigners, including rumors of fugitives from Lygos carrying something valuable.The Claws maimed most of Stonetop's militia to show they meant business.Lenox and the Grateful dealt with the threat to their new home by poisoning the Claws.Brennan escaped, and is rumored to be recruiting, maybe putting together new Claws.
Secrets - Brennan

characters/npcs/golenthi-senka-(dead).ht.title: Golenthi Senka (Dead)
characters/npcs/golenthi-senka-(dead).ht.description:
The previous Lightbearer from Stonetop. She travelled to Marshedge to do battle with a demon of the river. Died fighting the demon 31 years ago. Remembered as a martyr by her followers.
Mother to Aurelia Senka, by an unknown father

characters/npcs/hethenar.html.title: Hethenar
characters/npcs/hethenar.html.description: A priest of Helior in Stonetop.Raised Aurelia

characters/npcs/judicious-ackord.html.title: Judicious Ackord
characters/npcs/judicious-ackord.html.description:
Son of Studious
Father to Steadfast and Worthy.

characters/npcs/magistrate-ackord.html.title: Magistrate Ackord
characters/npcs/magistrate-ackord.html.description:
Authority of Aratis (something like the High Judge, at least within Stonetop)Son of Studious
Twin to Judicious
Uncle to Steady and Worthy AckordMarried. His wife recently gave birth to their third son.
His judgement of Lenox and his gang, the Grateful, was considered lenient.

characters/npcs/studious-ackord-(dead).h.title: Studious Ackord (Dead)
characters/npcs/studious-ackord-(dead).h.description: Judge, Chronicler in his day.father to Magistrate and Judicious Ackord

characters/npcs/the-grateful.html.title: The Grateful
characters/npcs/the-grateful.html.description: Lygosi drug smugglers who came to the edge of the world thinking they'd set themselves up as kingpins. Ended up using up their own supply and saved by the kindness of Stonetop.Eager, gullible Misses their family Most drawn to TorLittle, animal lover Missing finger, scars Most drawn to DanuNaive, kind widower, skinnyRookie, big Whistles, whittles Most drawn to HeliorBig, Reckless Red in the face, sings, snoresProud, popular Reliable, too serious Most drawn to AratisLed by Lenox Fyle

characters/npcs/urbgen-(dead).html.title: Urbgen (Dead)
characters/npcs/urbgen-(dead).html.description: We don't like to talk about it.

characters/npcs/worthy-ackord.html.title: Worthy Ackord
characters/npcs/worthy-ackord.html.description:
Son of Judicious Ackord.
Brother to Steady. Younger by 13 years.His twin and mother died during his birth.
His best friend's death is blamed on the actions of The Grateful.

characters/pcs/aurelia-senka.html.title: Aurelia Senka
characters/pcs/aurelia-senka.html.description:
https://hearthfire.camp/game/ThPTrnJaqcaPVYg6UcjL/lightbearer
Her mother Golenthi was a famous Lightbearer that died battling a demon near Marshedge.Born in Marshedge, brought back to Stonetop, her mother's hometown, following Golenthi's death. Goes with her eyes covered, and sometimes needs assistance around town, but wanders often in the Great Wood, sometimes for days at a time.Goat's milk soap is her favorite.As Lightbearer, she serves a spiritual role, especially for Helior worshippers. A small contingent of her mother's followers came with her as a baby to Stonetop. Are they still here? Her religious role include serving as a confessor. Her ability to abjure spirits might send villagers to her seeking "exorcisms."
Raised by Hethenar
Daughter to Golenthi Senka (Dead)
Crosses paths with River when they both wander the vicinity of Stonetop, and trade for milk from River's goats.

characters/pcs/lenox-fyle.html.title: Lenox Fyle
characters/pcs/lenox-fyle.html.description:
https://hearthfire.camp/game/ThPTrnJaqcaPVYg6UcjL/marshal
Came with The Grateful from Lygos, where they were a gang of otash addicts. The ripped off a dealer's stash and fled to the edge of the world, and Stonetop.They tried to sell otash in Stonetop but the people were poorer and their supply more finite than they counted on, and they used most of it themselves.
The villagers, even Judge Magistrate Ackord, forgave rather than punished, and even helped the band recover through withdrawals, earning their intense gratitude.
When Brennan and the Claws menaced Stonetop, maiming most of its informal militia as a warning, Lenox and the Grateful dealt with the threat by poisoning most of the Claws. Brennan escaped.The Grateful stepped into the role of a standing militia for Stonetop following the incident with the Claws.They are not trained soldiers but are street-smart and scrappy enough to break up fights and discourage conflict from getting out of hand.
Leader of The Grateful, a band of penitent smugglers from Lygos turned Stonetop militia.
River left food for the Lenox and the Grateful when the citizens of Stonetop nursed them through withdrawals.

characters/pcs/river.html.title: River
characters/pcs/river.html.description:
https://hearthfire.camp/game/ThPTrnJaqcaPVYg6UcjL/blessedA human raised in the Great Wood. Her parents lived among the Forest Folk.She doesn't have the distinctive eyes of those with Forest Folk ancestry, but there's a shifting quality to her hazel eyes that still makes people talk.Feels a strong connection to the earth, and often goes barefoot.Gifted with the knack for talking with beasts and spirits. Do villagers believe this is the blessing of Danu, or a Forest Folk craft she learned the trick of?The children of Stonetop like her better than the adults, many of whom find her strange, if not spooky. Deep water is dangerous. Everyone knows this.Gives tribute at the shrine of Danu.River lives at the edge of town, where she keeps goats. She contributes milk and cheese as well as meat and pelts. from hunting?Hunters from Stonetop seek her guidance when headed into the Wood.River's parents were humans living among the Forest Folk. One stormy night when she was a child, they went out and never returned.Bramble, Moss, and Pebble are her mastiffs.
River remembers Shep being kind to her when she arrived in Stonetop, seemingly an orphan. She was the first there for him when he returned from his violent exploits.
Crosses paths with Aurelia Senka when they both wander in the vicinity of Stonetop.
Provides Steadfast with certain animal goods specifically for rites of Aratis.
Left food for Lenox and The Grateful while they were in the midst of otash withdrawals.

characters/pcs/shep-marlowe.html.title: Shep Marlowe
characters/pcs/shep-marlowe.html.description:
https://hearthfire.camp/game/ThPTrnJaqcaPVYg6UcjL/heavyGood-hearted, but a determination to help led to a habit of getting involved in other people's business, which led to a habit of getting in fights.Left Stonetop for many years, possibly after a particular incident of violence went too far. Stories of him from the surrounding area filtered back in his absence. How old was he when he left? How long was he gone?Continued to attract more trouble and violence in his time away, seemingly more than even he could stomach. Seems to view his return to Stonetop and the hard but peaceful work at the forge a sort of retirement.His dreams are haunted by his past, and things darker still.The dreams worsened after he was struck by lightning, which villagers see as an obvious sign from Tor, and only increase the rumor swirling around him.Everyone loves to talk about the time he was struck by lightning, and woke up covered in glowing runic marks.
They're less keen to discuss what happened to Urbgen, even if he did have it coming.Refers to his time exploits away from Stonetop as "The War." Euphemistically? Diffusing with humor?Shep is the smith for Stonetop. The village relies upon his forge for all their metalwork, a huge responsibility. He buries himself in the work, and sometimes forgets to eat.In his youth, he was always willing to step in to break up (or at least finish) a fight or send off a ruffian. Does he abstain from that kind of thing, now that Stonetop has a dedicated militia?
A young Shep was among River's first connections in Stonetop after her parents disappeared.

characters/pcs/steadfast-of-the-ackord.h.title: Steadfast of the Ackord
characters/pcs/steadfast-of-the-ackord.h.description:
https://hearthfire.camp/game/ThPTrnJaqcaPVYg6UcjL/judgeCalled Steady informally (she prefers formality)From Clan Ackord. They are one of Stonetop's oldest families, believed to have been among its founders. They also have a long tradition in the priesthood of Aratis the Law-Giver.40 years old. Imposing. Red hair starting to go silver.Has made a lifelong special project of studying the Old Wall, and organizing the reclamation of its stone for new village structures.Trained as an acolyte since age 14, inspired by her father and uncle.Newly ordained as a full Judge, Steadfast is empowered to settle disputes among villagers that they cannot settle themselves.Judges are also historians of their jurisdiction, and Steady helps keep the Chronicle.
Daughter to Judicious Ackord
Niece to Magistrate Ackord
Sister to Worthy Ackord
Receives animal goods for Aratis rights from River.

places/lygos.html.title: Lygos
places/lygos.html.description:
Picture a sun-drenched land, a semi-arid climate. Roads stretch out between cities and oases. Farmers tend to orchards of figs, dates, and olives. Boundless fields of grain sway in gentle winds.Picture palaces, temples, and handsome estates. Priests, scholars, and bureaucrats bustle about. Politicians squabble over laws and votes. Merchants hawk goods from the far corners of the world. Dozens of languages can be heard in streets and taverns.Picture armies on the march in tight formation, spears and shields and helms a-glinting. Plumes of dust rise from thousands of stamping feet. Horses neigh and harnesses clatter. Camels bray. Elephants trumpet.Picture opulence and splendor, silks and feathers, spices piled high in lurid color.Picture hunger and desperation, urchins risking a hand to steal a loaf of bread. Picture the rich and powerful above mundane concern. Picture the poor and downtrodden consumed by nothing but.Lygos lies at least 40 days of travel to the south from Stonetop, none of them easy.Lenox Fyle and The Grateful are from Lygos.
Otari is a popular intoxicant, there.

things/otash.html.title: Otash
things/otash.html.description: A drug made from otari, a southern plant with a pleasant stimulant effect, traditionally made into refreshing tea. Otari grows most commonly in desert oases and cannot normally grow in Stonetop's more northern climbs. It grows tall like bamboo but in flat green blades, looking almost like kelp.Otash is a waxy oil that can be refined from otari by baking at incredibly high heat. Otash wax can be smoked or eaten, though it's often tinctured into strong alcohol to be more palatable (probably most popular method among Stonetop customers, plus it stretches the supply).Otash causes manic euphoria, numbness to pain, loss of impulse control. Long term usage causes mood swings, paranoia, and shakes.

things/the-river-king-(banished).html.title: The River King (Banished)
things/the-river-king-(banished).html.description: The River King was a demon that lurked beneath the Dread River and plagued the town of Marshedge before being defeated by Golenthi Senka, who perished in the attempt.Few outside the church of Helior know much of it. If someone in Stonetop has ever heard of the River King, it's probably because the overheard name made a useful boogeyman: "Stay away from deep water, or the River King will throw you in his still and boil you down for his whiskey."

index.html.title: Index
index.html.description: This isn't meant to be exhaustive - just to keep track of details and connections established as we answer questions and establish lore and backstory.Right now, it's not an encyclopedia of lore, more like notes of what we establish that the lore doesn't say.

places/stonetop.html.title: Stonetop
places/stonetop.html.description:
Stonetop is your home. The village… is home to around 300 folks. It's a nice place, though poor. People look out for each other. is built around a massive standing stone of unknown origin, carved with faint runes. Lightning strikes the Stone often. stands at edge of the Great Wood. Villagers hunt and trap but—per a compact with the Forest Folk—never fell a living tree. lies in the World's End, a sparsely populated region, dotted with ruins. The nearest settlement is days away. Stonetop worships four main gods: Aratis, the Law-Giver
Danu, the Earth Mother Helior, the Dawn Bringer Tor, the Rain Bringer, the Thunderhead, and the Slayer of Beasts
Because of the Stone and the storms it draws, Stonetop is thought to be particularly blessed and chosen by Tor.
Around 300 souls live in Stonetop, or about 50 families. Everyone knows everyone else, at least by name and reputation. Most families have been here for many generations, tied together by kinship and marriage.The village supports only a few full-time tradesfolk: a smith, a tanner, a potter, a midwife, and a publican. (5 souls, plus 5-10 assistants/apprentices)Hunters and trappers ply the wood for meat and fur, and also forage for fruits, vegetables, mushrooms, and useable wood. Trappers produce much of the village's wealth, but hunters range farther and have more prestige. (10-20 souls) Farmers work the fields, producing the village's staple foods. Hard, physical work. Most practice "minor" trades on the side, like carpentry, stonecutting, thatching, husbandry, distilling, etc. (~75 souls) Homemakers keep the village running. They cook, clean, tend gardens, spin, weave, sow, mind children, practice a dozen minor trades, and otherwise manage a household. Families might have 2 or 3 homemakers each, from across generations. (~100 souls) Elders have retired from the fields or the rigors of homemaking, but still help as they can. Many still serve the village as keepers of lore and wisdom. (~25 souls) Children play and learn and grow. They also help with chores, tend livestock, chase birds from the fields, forage near the Stream, haul water, mind younger children, and so forth, gaining more and more responsibilities as they grow. (~100 souls)

things/spirits.html.title: Spirits
things/spirits.html.description: The physical world—this mortal realm of base matter and flesh—is but one reality.There is another, hidden reality. Arguably a truer reality. Here, spirits dwell.The spirit realm is filled with entities, especially those of the natural world.Each beast, each tree, each gust of wind or flickering flame—they all have spirits. So do the soil, the rocks, the mountains and the streams.Most of these spirits are quiet, slumbering or barely conscious or operating on a scale so alien as to be impenetrable to human minds.But some mortals can speak to them nonetheless, and goad them into action. Sometimes, these sleepers shift and mumble and stretch of their own accord.The most active spirits are those tethered to physical objects, or those associated with beasts or other "animate" things—things full of life and energy. These are the spirits that mortals encounter most often.

things/crinwin.html.title: Crinwin
things/crinwin.html.description:
Trust not thine ears, among the trees
Ignore the false and desperate pleas
Look you up and scan the skies
For snarling teeth and pale-dead eyes
Long of limb and gray of skin
Come the menace, the Crinwin
Imagine:
Out-of-place noises: partial bird calls, off-season insect buzz, a bear's growl from the treetops, snippets of nonsense speech
Figures scurrying, leaping, swinging through the branches
Sinewy strong fingers around your throat
Clammy, blackish blood; too cold and putrid to be natural
They've always been there, in the Wood, lurking in the trees. For generations, the Forest Folk hunted them and kept their numbers in check. No longer.They're humanoid, about half the size of a full-grown human, with elongated limbs, hairless heads and bodies, and vacant, dead-eyed faces.They mimic people. They can wear leaves like clothes, hold branches like tools, and even perfectly repeat snippets of speech, but show no understanding of language beyond what sounds can be used to lure prey, or scare off threats.They live and move in the upper branches of the Great Wood, where they build papery nests like giant wasps.
